steps: Paracetamol overdose: N-ACETYLCYSTEINE (use the nomogram / treat if staggered or uncertain timing).
Supportive care; monitor INR, glucose, lactate, creatinine and mental status for acute liver failure.
Contact a liver/transplant unit early if ALF criteria (rising INR, encephalopathy, acidosis) — King's College criteria.
Avoid further hepatotoxins; treat complications (coagulopathy, hypoglycaemia, cerebral oedema).

drugRefs.dose: 150 mg/kg over 1 h, then 50 mg/kg over 4 h, then 100 mg/kg over 16 h (21-hour regimen)
drugRefs.freq: continuous per regimen; continue if ongoing hepatotoxicity
drugRefs.why: Restores hepatic glutathione — antidote for paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity; treat per nomogram, or empirically if staggered/uncertain timing. Also benefits non-paracetamol acute liver failure.
Hypoglycaemia is common in acute liver failure and a treatable cause of deterioration.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Toxic and Drug-Induced Hepatitis / Acute Liver Failure
AASLD Position Paper — Management of Acute Liver Failure
King's College Criteria for liver transplantation in ALF

decision.label: Stop toxin; NAC for paracetamol; monitor for ALF

confirm: Acute transaminitis ± jaundice temporally linked to a drug/toxin (esp. paracetamol). Assess for acute liver failure (INR, encephalopathy).
